subject: Multiple groups: Can constrain 2 groups to be equal and 1 to vary?

messages.author: ab13cdb63d3ee740
messages.subject: Multiple groups: Can constrain 2 groups to be equal and 1 to vary?
parts:
Hi,
I know that at the parameter level, I can set an equality constraint or fixed value for 2 groups and allow the 3rd group's estimate be free to vary, but is there a way to do this across all loadings, intercepts, etc.? That is, is there a way to convey this through group.equal argument rather than typing c(a, a, NA) or something similar for every single loading path?

For example, if I find that I have noninvariance comparing the configural model to model with the group.equal = loadings argument, can I do a follow up that would allow me to see if I have invariant loadings for 2 of the 3 groups?  That is, apply group.equal for 2 groups on loadings but allow the 3rd group's loadings to be estimated/unconstrained?

Thanks,
Jill

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multiple groups: Can constrain 2 groups to be equal and 1 to vary?
parts: is there a way to convey this through group.equal argument rather than typing c(a, a, NA) or something similar for every single loading path?
No, group.equal= operates at the level of a parameter, applied across all groups.

if I find that I have noninvariance comparing the configural model to model with the group.equal = loadings argument, can I do a follow up that would allow me to see if I have invariant loadings for 2 of the 3 groups?  That is, apply group.equal for 2 groups on loadings but allow the 3rd group's loadings to be estimated/unconstrained?

That is an incredibly (Type I and II) error-prone data-driven procedure .  If an item functions differentially, it functions differentially.  I wouldn't recommend fishing around further, just leave it free.  Unless you actually have substantive theoretical reasons to expect 1 group to respond different to that item than the other 2 do.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: Multiple groups: Can constrain 2 groups to be equal and 1 to vary?
parts: In fact, we do have the hypothesis that 2 of the groups are similar, but both differ from the third. I am not sure why this would be worse than doing a follow up in ANOVA where the omnibus F is significant, and you do t tests to see how the groups differ. We’d just be doing one contrast (2 vs 1) to follow up an a priori hypothesis. It would seem to be a better way than collapsing the two groups together and assuming they are invariant.

parts: In fact, we do have the hypothesis that 2 of the groups are similar, but both differ from the third.
Then indeed, you should test your hypothesized pattern.

I am not sure why this would be worse than doing a follow up in ANOVA where the omnibus F is significant, and you do t tests to see how the groups differ. We’d just be doing one contrast (2 vs 1) to follow up an a priori hypothesis. It would seem to be a better way than collapsing the two groups together and assuming they are invariant.

I agree.  That was my "unless", which I didn't expand on because it is a refreshing situation that I rarely encounter.
